subject: Re: RBAC v2 — break-glass + support impersonation policy decision (Private)
body:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Hanae Suzuki <hanae.suzuki@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 11, 2025 at 9:18 AM PST
Subject: RBAC v2 — break-glass + support impersonation policy decision (Private)

Aisha,

We need an explicit leadership decision for RBAC v2 rollout re: break-glass safeguards and whether we allow Support impersonation for Private customers.

Context:
- Break-glass plumbing is landing (time-bounded elevated session + explicit audit events).
- Enterprise questionnaires are now asking: “Can Support impersonate in Private?” and “What controls exist to prevent abuse?”
- Private deployments add complexity (customer-managed environment; can be air-gapped).

Decision points for you:
1) Support impersonation in Private: default OFF vs allow with controls (and what controls?)
2) Break-glass approvals: who can grant, max duration, monitoring expectations
3) Evidence expectations (what we must be able to show for SOC2/ISO and customer reviews)

I’ve attached a short memo with options + recommended path.

Attachment: RBACv2_BreakGlass_Safeguards_Decision_Memo_v1.2.pdf

Marcus Lin
Security Engineering (Exec Owner)
Redwood Inference


---

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Hanae Suzuki <hanae.suzuki@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 11, 2025 at 10:07 AM PST
Subject: Re: RBAC v2 — break-glass + support impersonation policy decision (Private)

Adding SRE view:

We do need a reliable “get us unstuck” path during incidents, but we should not conflate that with impersonation.

What has worked elsewhere:
- Break-glass = elevated session to perform a specific class of admin actions (e.g., unblock user, rollback config, view system health), time-boxed (30–60 min), with immediate alerting to Security + on-call lead.
- Separate workflow for “act as user” (impersonation) because it’s higher risk and harder to justify.

If we allow impersonation at all in Private, I’d want:
- Explicit customer opt-in (contractual + technical config)
- Per-incident customer approval or ticket reference, captured in audit log
- Short TTL, and forced reason code
- Monitoring + weekly review report to Security

Net: we can meet incident requirements without user impersonation for 95%+ of cases.

Sean Gallagher
SRE Lead (Workflows)


---

From: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Hanae Suzuki <hanae.suzuki@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 11, 2025 at 11:22 AM PST
Subject: Re: RBAC v2 — break-glass + support impersonation policy decision (Private)

On evidence + auditability:

If we choose to allow any break-glass / impersonation path, we must ensure events are unambiguous and exportable.

Minimum for each authorization decision and each elevated session event:
- actor_user_id + actor_email
- actor_role_ids
- decision allow/deny + reason_code
- policy_version
- session_id (if break-glass)
- elevation_grantor (who approved it) + approval_reference (ticket)
- target identifiers (org_id, project_id; and if impersonation, target_user_id)

We also need to define retention and access controls for viewing these logs (who can view exported audit logs, and whether this itself is gated behind Security Admin vs Org Admin).

Attaching sample schema fields we’ve been using in PR review.

Attachment: AuthzDecision_AuditLog_Fields_Sample.json

Kevin Osei
Audit Logging Lead


---

From: Hanae Suzuki <hanae.suzuki@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 11, 2025 at 12:03 PM PST
Subject: Re: RBAC v2 — break-glass + support impersonation policy decision (Private)

Private-specific constraints:

- Some Private customers will be air-gapped. Anything requiring Redwood-hosted approval services or always-on connectivity won’t work.
- We can implement technical gating in the Private installer/config:
  - Support impersonation feature flag default disabled and not exposed in UI.
  - To enable, customer must explicitly set a config value and provision a dedicated “support access” identity provider group mapping.
- For “break-glass” we can implement customer-local approvals (e.g., customer admin grants an elevated session) but that’s different from Redwood Support using our internal tooling.

Recommendation: for Private, do not support “Support impersonation” in GA. We can offer a controlled “support session” mode that allows limited diagnostic actions, not full user-level access.

Hanae Suzuki
Secure Defaults (Private)

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Hanae Suzuki <hanae.suzuki@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 12, 2025 at 8:41 AM PST
Subject: Re: RBAC v2 — break-glass + support impersonation policy decision (Private)

Support ops input:

We get recurring asks like “Can you reproduce this in our UI as our admin?”

In Hosted/Dedicated, impersonation has been a blunt instrument. It solves some issues quickly but it’s also where customers get nervous.

For Private:
- I’m OK with a clear “no impersonation” stance as long as we give Support something workable:
  - ability to request customer to share audit log extracts
  - limited read-only diagnostics (health, config snapshots, version info)
  - guided steps for customer admins to execute sensitive actions

But we should be explicit in customer-facing language; otherwise, Sales will keep getting pulled into “we thought you could just log in and fix it” escalations.

Dev Patel
Support Ops

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Hanae Suzuki <hanae.suzuki@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 12, 2025 at 2:16 PM PST
Subject: Re: RBAC v2 — break-glass + support impersonation policy decision (Private)

For rollout/migration planning:

If decision is “no impersonation for Private,” we should bake it into:
- RBAC v2 default roles (Support role should not include any “impersonate:*” permissions in Private policy bundle)
- Migration comms + docs (so customers don’t assume parity with Hosted)
- Runbooks (SRE + Support) so incident procedures don’t rely on impersonation

If we do want an exception path, we need to define it now because it impacts policy bundle packaging and feature flags.

Connor O'Brien
Release / Migration Lead


---

From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Hanae Suzuki <hanae.suzuki@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 13, 2025 at 4:47 PM PST
Subject: Re: RBAC v2 — break-glass + support impersonation policy decision (Private)

Decision (effective for RBAC v2 GA scope):

1) Support impersonation for Private deployments: NOT permitted by default; not supported in GA.
- Rationale: disproportionate risk in customer-managed environments + hard to evidence controls reliably (especially air-gapped).
- Any request to enable impersonation in Private is treated as an exception requiring CISO approval and contractual language. Treat this as “roadmap / custom” rather than standard capability.

2) Break-glass (all tiers): permitted with strict safeguards.
Minimum safeguards:
- Time-bounded elevated session (max 60 minutes) with forced reason code.
- Approval required from (a) Security exec owner or delegate + (b) on-call lead (SRE) when invoked for incident response. For non-incident requests, approval from Security exec owner + Support ops lead.
- Approval reference must be captured (INT-/SUP- ticket or incident ID).
- Immediate notifications: #eng-security and on-call channel; include actor, scope, duration, approval reference.
- Post-use review within 2 business days by Security (spot check against reason + actions taken).

3) Monitoring + evidence expectations:
- All authz decisions for privileged actions must carry policy_version, role_ids, decision_reason, and session_id when elevated.
- Audit events for “elevation granted / started / ended” are mandatory.
- We need a weekly report (automated is fine) of all break-glass sessions: who/when/why/what scope; Security reviews.

Action items:
- Marcus: update the internal support-break-glass-access policy doc with this decision + approval matrix.
- Kevin: confirm audit log schema supports approval_reference + session_id across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
- Hanae: ensure Private installer defaults do not expose impersonation configuration, and docs state the limitation clearly.
- Connor: incorporate into RBAC v2 migration plan + customer-facing security questionnaire responses.

If anyone believes we have a material blocker for incident response without Private impersonation, bring a concrete scenario; otherwise proceed.

Dr. Aisha Rahman
CISO
Redwood Inference
